title: Cognitive Fatigue in Autoregressive Transformers: Formalization and Measurement
claim: A lightweight diagnostic built from three inference-time signals under explicit axioms is validated across multiple empirical stress tests.
layout: 4 panels (a)-(d), left-to-right, dashed arrows linking inputs, core, evidence
description: A wide four-column figure with rounded cards on a white background. Panel (a), Inputs, is a column of three peach boxes: Prompt + Context, Model Family & Decoding, and Probes. Panel (b), Measurement Core, is the largest. It holds three purple boxes (Prompt Attention, Entropy Deviation, Embedding Drift) with their notation. A dashed gray Evaluation Data box is labeled "Evaluation Only". A blue Fatigue Index box shows the formula FI = w_aΦ_a(A) + w_eΦ_e(E) + w_dΦ_d(D). Panel (c), Axioms & Properties, is a row of five gray numbered tiles under the core. Panel (d), Evidence & Findings, is a column of four color-coded cards: green, purple, orange and red. Gray dashed arrows run left to right between panels. The eye goes first to the center formula and the colored signal boxes.
caption: Overview of the cognitive fatigue measurement framework. (a) A prompt and context are fed to a decoder-only model, with probes extracting attention logits and hidden states. (b) Three signals are computed online at each decoding step: prompt-attention decay, entropy deviation, and embedding drift, normalized and aggregated into the Fatigue Index (FI). Evaluation datasets are used only to validate FI, not to compute it. (c) FI is grounded in five axioms: monotonicity, scale invariance, boundedness, stability, and compositionality. (d) FI is validated against repetition and F1 drop, precision stress (FP16 vs. 4-bit), long-context (varying input length) stress, and scaling behavior across nine models from 1B to 13B parameters.
abstract: Autoregressive language models frequently degrade during long-horizon generation, producing repetitive text, losing instruction adherence, and exhibiting unstable entropy. Despite the prevalence of these failures, practitioners lack online diagnostics to detect them in real-time as they occur. We formalize this degradation as cognitive fatigue, a measurable generation-time state characterized by decay in attention to the original prompt, representational drift, and entropy miscalibration. We introduce the Fatigue Index (FI), a lightweight, model-agnostic diagnostic that aggregates these three signals under explicit axioms (monotonicity, boundedness, interpretability) enabling reliable runtime monitoring. Across nine models (1B-13B parameters), FI trajectories exhibit structured temporal dynamics, predict task degradation (AUROC = 0.95) and repetition (Spearman rho = 0.94), and reveal non-monotonic scaling behavior: instruction-tuned models below 3B exhibit faster collapse than base models, with this trend reversing at 7B. Stress analyses further show that FI onset accelerates under longer contexts, middle-positioned evidence, and reduced numerical precision. These results establish cognitive fatigue as a coherent and measurable phenomenon, and position FI as a principled tool for runtime reliability monitoring in production LLM systems.
